text.tspan: Everyday English - B2 - 2026/06/15 - Essay - 01
A calendar gives plans a place in time.
Pexels · 20657557
Looking back and looking ahead
A good way to make a realistic plan combines practical structure with an awareness of other people. Neither a rigid plan nor complete
improvisation is sufficient on its own; both need to be judged in context.
The practical case is straightforward: reviewing a specific experience teaches more than a vague judgement. Consider how we describe one
habit that helped us instead of calling the whole year good or bad. The benefit is not merely efficiency. A modest arrangement prevents
avoidable confusion, leaving attention available for the activity itself rather than for problems that could have been anticipated.
Consideration adds a second, equally important dimension: a small next step is easier to act on than a broad promise. In this situation, we
choose a ten-minute practice session and put it on the calendar. A decision can be convenient for one person while creating difficulty for
another, so its value depends partly on whose needs it recognises.
The most useful approach therefore brings structure and consideration together. Preparation establishes a workable starting point; attention to
other people keeps it responsive. Success should be assessed by how well the arrangement serves the experience, rather than by how
closely events follow the original plan.
BUILD YOUR OWN · State a clear main idea; develop two different points with examples; bring them together in the conclusion. Each body
paragraph needs a distinct point and a concrete example. The conclusion should connect the argument rather than introduce a new proposal.
Identify two obstacles that could arise when people make a realistic plan. Explain a workable response to each, rather than merely listing the
problems. Use four short paragraphs: introduction, two developed points, and conclusion. (Model: One possible outline: introduce the
situation; discuss reviewing a specific experience teaches more than a vague judgement with an example; discuss a small next step is easier
to act on than a broad promise with a different example; conclude by connecting the two points.)
